signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD outperforms the G10 peer group with a 1W average gain of +1.081% across 4 pairs, while JPY lags as the weakest currency at -0.667% across 7 pairs, establishing a 1.748% leader-to-laggard spread. RBA cash rate sits at 4.60% (HIKING) against BoJ at 1.25% (HIKING), leaving an authoritative OIS carry spread of +337bp favoring AUD on AONIA-TONA basis (+335bp policy spread). Intraday spot trades at 110.715 with VIX contained at 17.6 (normal volatility), allowing carry flows to dominate. Crude and geopolitical headlines from the Strait of Hormuz keep oil near $98.1, insulating commodity-linked AUD against broader growth drag while keeping Japanese terms-of-trade under structural pressure. Reversal risk in USD/JPY technical structure warns of potential JPY consolidation, but cross carry maintains upside pressure above 110.00. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/JPY, sustained by +337bp OIS carry advantage and G10 divergence. Catalyst: Japan Trade Balance release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sudden risk-off spike pushing VIX above 25, triggering disorderly carry unwinds.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Intervention Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.19, holding above its SMA20 (157.97) and SMA50 (157.70) while testing the SMA200 at 158.56. Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% maintains a 275bp policy rate advantage for USD, reflected in an OIS carry premium of +265bp (SOFR 3.88% vs TONA 1.23%). The options market diverges sharply from spot resilience, with 1M 25d risk reversals printing at -1.93, showing pronounced put skew as downside protection is aggressively bid. Heightened Strait of Hormuz naval tensions and Brent holding near $110 keep energy import vulnerability elevated for Japan, yet speculative positioning remains net short JPY at -37,820 contracts (88th percentile of its 52-week range). Spot at 158.19 sits in sensitive territory where 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered MoF verbal warnings and heightened intervention risk. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY, carry-supported while VIX remains contained at 17.6. Catalyst: BoJ policy meeting 30 Oct. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 prompting official Ministry of Finance market intervention.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Inflection + Rate Spread
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3376, pushing above its SMA20 (1.3249) while testing overhead resistance at the SMA50 (1.3414) and SMA200 (1.3434) cluster. Fed at 4.00% vs BoE at 3.75% yields a tight 25bp policy spread in USD's favor (+15bp OIS basis), while UK 10Y gilts offer 5.44% against US 10Y at 5.132% (+30bp spread). UK unemployment falling to 4.7% with earnings holding at 3.7% reinforces BoE rate resilience, supporting GBP performance (1W avg +0.691% across 4 pairs). Trend structure indicates a short-term reversal against the prior downtrend, confirmed by a bullish wide-range bar and a break above the 10-day closing high. A daily close above the SMA50/SMA200 band at 1.3414/1.3434 is required to establish structural trend continuation toward 1.3500. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD, supported by resilient UK labor data and gilt yield support. Catalyst: UK CPI release on 21 Oct at 06:00 UTC (consensus 2.7% y/y). Risk: UK headline CPI missing forecasts significantly, shifting BoE expectations toward cuts.
